quotes.colour_meaning: alerts of green (little or no impact), yellow (regional impact and response), orange (national-scale impact and response), and red (international response)

pager_alert_levels.interpretation_note: These are USGS-published PAGER Earthquake Impact Scale thresholds. They are used only to interpret PAGER colour levels. They are not contract attachment levels, not insured-industry-loss figures, and are never used as contract X. The seven-bin probability distributions in losspager alerts.json are a separate, finer published product; this section quotes the four-colour EIS table from the background page, not a rescaling of those bins.

three_way_separation.statement: PAGER economic loss, insured industry loss, and bond principal impairment are three strictly separate quantities. PAGER economic loss (alert colour, published probability bins, and any empirical point estimate) is a USGS modelled economic figure; it is never used as contract X. Insured industry loss X is a contractual industry index (for example PCS or PERILS) or an equivalent settlement input; it is not configured in Phase 1 and is licensed when it exists. Bond principal impairment is min(1, max(0, (X-A)/(E-A))) and is numeric only when X, A and E are all verified on a verified overlapping bond.

pager_historical.description: Comparison events are listed as published in the USGS losspager product (historical_earthquakes.json, and the historical_comment in comments.json when present). Nothing is added from memory.

catalog_analogs.status: our own choice (d), not a USGS rule
catalog_analogs.description: M >= 6.0 events within 250 km of the epicentre since 1900-01-01, queried from the USGS FDSN event API, excluding the event itself (and its associated USGS ids). Up to the five largest are listed, plus a count of all matches. Distances are a haversine calculation by this tool (d) using a mean Earth radius of 6371 km. The radius, magnitude floor, start year and 'five largest' cap are screening choices of this tool, not a USGS rule.

caveats: The USGS catalog is incomplete before modern instrumentation, and early 20th-century magnitudes, locations and completeness vary.

PAGER historical comparisons are listed as published. They are not a complete regional catalog; PAGER place names and country codes (for example Name=UK) are shown as in the product and are not independently recoded.
PAGER historical comparison times are often published without a timezone suffix and are shown as published.
No insured-loss figures, PCS/PERILS values, or bond outcomes are included in historical comps.

pager_economic_usd.status: used for public site and alert figures
pager_economic_usd.label: USGS PAGER modelled economic loss (all losses, not insured, not a bond trigger)

bin_conversion.statement: Raw losspager alerts.json (and pager.xml) economic bin edges 0, 1, 10, 100, 1000, 10000, 100000, 10000000 are in USD millions. Converted min_usd / max_usd = raw_edge × 1,000,000. The alerts.json units field is 'USD' and does not itself say 'millions'; the millions scale was verified against the product and the published Earthquake Impact Scale (see evidence).
evidence: The PAGER one-pager PDF (onepager.pdf) labels the estimated-economic-loss histogram axis 'USD (Millions)'. Verified on us6000u43g (M7.0 Nagqu, PAGER version 8) on 2026-11-12 by extracting text from the published PDF.

The PAGER Earthquake Impact Scale (https://earthquake.usgs.gov/data/pager/background.php) states economic colour thresholds as green < $1 million, yellow $1 million–$100 million, orange $100 million–$1 billion, red $1 billion+. These match the seven published bin edges under a millions interpretation (0–1 green; 1–10 and 10–100 yellow; 100–1000 orange; 1000+ red).

Empirical point estimates (losses.json empirical_economic.total_dollars, published in USD) fall in the highest-probability bin only when edges are read as millions: us6000u43g $301,381,391 is in 100–1000 million (orange, p≈0.35); us6000tjl2 $8,159,004,208 is in 1000–10000 million (red, p≈0.33); us7000tx16 $32 is in 0–1 million (green). The raw-USD reading (edges as dollars) cannot place $301 million in 100–1000 or $32 in 0–1.
bin_conversion.source_of_raw_edges: losspager alerts.json (and the same edges in pager.xml)

quantiles.status: own calculation (d), not a USGS published range
quantiles.method: From the published economic-bin probabilities, form a cumulative distribution (probabilities are renormalized to sum to 1, which is this tool's own choice (d) to absorb published rounding residuals). The quantile q is located in the bin whose cumulative interval contains q. Inside that bin the loss is interpolated in log space: if the bin is [L, U] with incoming cumulative F_L and mass p, x = L * (U/L)^((q - F_L)/p). This is equivalent to treating log(loss) as uniform within the bin. When a published lower edge is 0, L is replaced by 1 USD for the logarithm only (this floor is our own choice (d); the q=0 edge stays the published 0). The last published upper edge is used as the finite cap; no further tail is invented. The point estimate is not an input to this calculation — only the bin probabilities and converted edges are.

point_estimate.unavailable: If the field is missing, the value is 'unavailable: <reason>'. A published 0 is 0, not unavailable.

display.compact_units: Values under 1,000 USD are shown as whole dollars; then k, m, bn, tn (thousands, millions, billions, trillions). Millions and billions of 100 or more are rounded to the nearest whole unit (301m); 10–99 to a whole unit (27bn); under 10 to one decimal (3.3m, 8.2bn). The tilde marks a model estimate. This is a display rule only; stored USD figures are not rounded this way.

pager_economic_usd.three_way_reminder: These USD figures are USGS PAGER modelled economic loss (all losses). They are not insured industry loss and not a bond-impairment figure, and they are never used as contract X.

tc_assumptions.status: used for storms.json only (demo/example); own calculations marked (d)
tc_assumptions.label: demo/example

methods.label: Zone entry (d)
methods.value: first crossing of a track (fixes joined by straight lines in lon/lat) with the zone outline

methods.label: ensemble fraction (d)
methods.value: members whose track enters the zone divided by members in the file, per initialisation
methods.note: Not a calibrated probability. Never blended or added with official NHC products. The mean track is never used alone.

methods.label: Closest approach (d)
methods.value: minimum distance from the track, densified every 5 km, to the zone outline (0 inside); local equirectangular km, Earth radius 6371 km

methods.label: Intensity at entry (d)
methods.value: pressure (hPa) and wind (kt) linearly interpolated in time to the entry time; NHC wind = one-minute sustained at 10 m (NHC glossary); Weather Lab wind averaging period not stated

methods.label: Forecast horizon
methods.value: 120 h for both NHC advisories and Weather Lab members (Google tracks thinned to 120 h)

caveats: ensemble fraction is the share of ensemble members entering a zone, not a calibrated probability.
Cone is not the wind, surge or rain footprint. It shows the probable track of the storm centre.

Google DeepMind Weather Lab cyclone tracks are experimental research data, not official, and not an officially supported Google product. Historical data (1 h or more old) are CC BY 4.0; only such data are published.
Zones are coarse display approximations (simplified country outlines), not contractual coverage, grids or boxes. Entry into a land outline is not the contractual test.
A track entering a zone is a watch condition, not a payout. REPORTED TRIGGER OUTCOME is used only when a public source reports the outcome, cited.
Bond fields on TC zones are a public summary, not verified against offering circular.
No payout scale, trigger-grid geometry, risk statistics, pricing or loss figures are published.
